## My thinking this year

I'm 61 now. My wife and I manage this bit of land, 7.7 mu — our son works in town so he sends a little money but doesn't help much in the field. I only started farming seriously two years ago after I came back from working outside, so honest truth, I mostly do what my older brother and my neighbors tell me. They've been farming this same ground their whole lives. I watch what they do.

Last year the wheat was alright, about 400 kg per mu I'd say, and the maize was decent too, maybe a bit over 450. Nothing special, but we didn't lose money. This year I'll do about the same — no reason to change when it worked.

**Wheat** goes in around early-mid October, right after the maize comes off. I plow once with the small tractor I hire from old Wang down the lane — costs me about 40 yuan per mu but I can't afford my own machine. For fertilizer I use the compound stuff, the 15-15-15 bag, maybe two bags per mu before planting, and then when the wheat starts jointing in spring I put down another bag of urea, maybe 15 kg on each mu. That's what the shopkeeper told me and my neighbor does the same. I water it before winter, then once at jointing, and once more when the grain is filling — three times, using my neighbor's well, costs me for the electricity. My seed I buy from the agro-shop, the common variety, nothing fancy.

**Maize** goes straight in after the wheat harvest in mid-June. No time for deep plowing — maybe a week if I'm lucky. I just use the no-till planter a custom operator runs through the village, 30 yuan per mu, drops seed and a bit of starter fertilizer all at once. Then when the maize is about knee-high I topdress urea, about one bag (roughly 15 kg) per mu. I irrigate maybe once or twice if it doesn't rain enough — usually the summer rains help. Harvest late September.

I don't buy much pesticide. Some herbicide for the wheat in spring because the weeds get bad, and once in a while I'll spray something on the maize if I see those worms in the tassels. My wife and I do most of the work ourselves. At harvest I pay the combine operator — can't do that by hand at my age.

Money's tight. We have maybe 3,000 yuan cash for the whole year's inputs, and I try not to spend more than that. If I had more I might use better seed or more fertilizer, but this is what we can manage.
